gaps: Every breath-one item treated death as the cash reaching zero and looked for mis-scheduled steps and mis-counted counterparties. Sharpening Watched burn against The front produced a runway whose length depends on its being read, and Cost of the coffin put the death line above zero. This produced the changed question for breath two: whether the clock is cash at all, and which runways change length when counted.
accepted: Date bomb: an obligation that arrives as a step rather than a slope, as the lease that renews in September, the annual premium, the tax bill in April, the tuition due before the school year, so the death is at the first step the balance cannot clear and not at the month the average burn predicts; the carrier is the calendar, the cash figure misreads a staircase as a ramp, and a better count corrects it, since the schedule was always on paper; the seasonal case, the fisherman's winter or the nine-month salary, is the same staircase repeated.

Reach the cliff: an asset that arrives as a step, as the vesting date, the pension's twentieth year, the bonus paid in March, the tranche released on a milestone, naturalization at year five, so the runway is not a number of months but a race whose prize is a jump, and the whole loss is quitting three weeks early; the carrier is the payer's schedule, the cash figure misreads a binary as a slope, since the months before the cliff are worth nothing on their own and everything as a bridge; not Date bomb, which is a step down, and the correction is counting to the date, not counting months.

Cash behind glass: money that is owned but cannot be reached in time, as deposits at a bank taken into receivership on a Friday, a retirement account behind a penalty, a receivable held in escrow, savings in a currency that cannot leave its country, so the runway runs on the reachable balance and the pipe's delay rather than on the owned one; the carrier is the pipe between the account and the payroll, the cash figure counts ownership where the clock runs on access, and a better count corrects it once the ledger has an access column, which it usually does not.

Burn you cannot put down: burn divides into what stops when you stop it and what stops only after notice, severance, or a lease's remaining term, so two firms with equal burn have unequal runways under cuts, and the first cut costs a step before it saves a slope; the carrier is the stack of commitments, the cash figure misreads one number for what is a floor and a ceiling, and a better count corrects it, since each commitment carries its notice period on paper; not Date bomb, which is one step on the calendar, since this is the shape of the whole burn under the operator's own hand.

Cost of the coffin: dying costs money, as the final payroll, the accrued leave, the lease break, the deposits returned, the accountant who closes the books, so the line at which a firm must stop is not zero but zero plus the cost of stopping cleanly, and the founder who runs the balance to nothing has already crossed it; the carrier is the wind-down bill, the cash figure misreads zero for the floor, and a better count corrects it; the creditor's covenant that calls the loan at a minimum balance draws the same line from outside, and sits here rather than under Watched burn because it is a written number, not an inference.

Near the pole: runway is cash over net burn, and net burn is the difference of two large flows, so two operators with identical months differ by how close their burn sits to the pole where income covers it, as a shop taking in ninety and spending a hundred has the same three months as a startup taking in nothing and spending ten, and only the shop can multiply its runway by a ten-percent cut; the carrier is the ratio of the gross flows to their difference, the cash figure misreads a point for the steepness of the curve the point sits on, and counting corrects it, but only if the gross flows are counted and not the net.

Receivable from the dying: money owed to you by a customer whose own clock runs on your weather, as the subcontractor owed by a builder in a housing bust or the freelancer owed by the agency that lost the same client, so the receivable is a loan to someone whose death is correlated with yours, and it arrives as cash when least needed and as a loss when most; the carrier is the customer's balance sheet, the cash figure misreads a dated claim for cash to come, and a better count corrects the ageing but not the correlation, which appears only when the customer's runway is counted too.

Forbearance clock: a debt with no schedule, as the family loan, the supplier who lets the invoice slide, the tax authority that has not yet noticed, the credit line uncalled, is due at the creditor's discretion, and the creditor's discretion runs on the creditor's own runway, so the debt is patient exactly until the creditor is in trouble, which is when you are; the carrier is the creditor's clock, the cash figure misreads an uncalled debt as not due, and no count of your own ledger corrects it, since the due date lives in someone else's; Receivable from the dying on the other side of the sheet.

Watched burn: a burn that counterparties can see is repriced as they see it, as the landlord who asks for a larger deposit, the supplier who moves to cash on delivery, the investor who reads the bank statement, the buyer whose diligence finds the runway and waits for the price to fall, so terms tighten as the clock shortens and shorten it further; the carrier is the counterparties' inference from what they can observe, the cash figure misreads terms as fixed when they are a function of the perceived clock, and the correction is not a better count of the ledger but a count of what others can see of it.

The front: a runway that runs on the belief that it is long, as the house with no cash behind it, the firm that pays every vendor late but on an exact schedule, the officer's mess bill, so credit flows as long as the belief does and the death arrives on the day of the discovery rather than the day of the zero; the carrier is others' belief used as collateral, the cash figure misreads the clock as continuous when it ends at a step set by an exposure, and no count corrects it, since the quantity is a belief; Watched burn with the sign reversed: there, being seen shortens, here, not being seen lengthens.

Lien of blood: savings that are yours on the statement and a family's in fact, as the immigrant whose balance is also a sibling's tuition and a parent's surgery, the couple whose joint account is one partner's runway and the other's veto, so the disposable balance is the statement minus every claim that will be made before the death and enforced by no one but you; the carrier is kinship claims on no ledger, the cash figure misreads ownership for disposability, and counting the claims corrects it, which most people can do and do not; the parents' spare room, on no ledger and lengthening the clock at a price in standing, is the same carrier with the sign flipped, and its price belongs to the status maps.

The back: the body is the asset that produces the income and is drawn down by producing it, as the carpenter's back, the nurse's nights, the surgeon's hands, the drummer's hearing, so the double shift that lengthens the cash runway spends the body's, and the two clocks run in opposite directions; the carrier is work capacity, the cash figure misreads the income as free of depreciation, and no count corrects it without a second ledger in a second unit, which is a change of what is counted; the ship's hull kept afloat by deferred repair is the firm's back, and comes due as a Date bomb with no date printed.

Any-town skill: a skill that is cash in any town lengthens the runway to the time it takes to move, while a skill that is cash only here shortens it to the cash, as the nurse or the welder against the fixer who knows this council, the session player known in this scene, the courtier; the carrier is the geography of the market for the skill, the cash figure misreads the pile for the pump, and it is corrected only by counting where the skill sells and at what discount, a change of quantity; adjacent to the floors under income, which the sibling map keeps, and adds only that the floor's location is what sets the clock.

residue.item: Wrong phase: a balance read at the wrong point of a seasonal income cycle, as the fisherman in winter or the academic in August.
residue.why: Merged into Date bomb: the same arithmetic error, a snapshot read against a flat burn, corrected by the same calendar; the seasonal case is now the staircase repeated in the bomb's discriminator.

residue.item: The couch: the parents' spare room, the parish, the regiment, a reserve that appears on no ledger and lengthens the clock at a price in standing.
residue.why: Merged into Lien of blood as the same carrier with the sign flipped; kept visible in the lien's discriminator because its price is in standing, which is the status maps' territory, and a separate item here would restate what they carry.

residue.item: Pipeline as runway: deals in progress counted as cash to come, whose close probability falls as the buyer's diligence finds the runway.
residue.why: Rejected: the counting part is a miscount of cash, not a misread by a correct count, and the mechanism part, the buyer who sees the burn and waits, is already Watched burn; kept as the boundary case.

residue.item: Covenant tripwire: a loan called at a minimum balance, so the firm dies at a number above zero set by a creditor.
residue.why: Merged into Cost of the coffin: the same line above zero, drawn from outside; the coffin's discriminator now says why it belongs there and not under Watched burn, since a covenant is a written number and not an inference.

gaps: The changed question yielded a loop the ledger cannot see from inside (Hurry discount), two clocks held by other people (Too expensive to let die, Weakest wallet), and two runways in units money does not buy (Stamp's clock, Runway in shots). The territory pointer 'runway illusions' stands and the slug is kept; the of-sentence now asks, for each item, whether a better count corrects it or only a change in what is counted, and the seriation answers in three grades rather than the pointer's two: inside your ledger, inside someone else's, and outside money.
accepted: Hurry discount: assets counted at what they would fetch with time to sell fetch less the less time there is, as the inventory, the machinery, the house, the domain name, so the runway sets the pile's price and the pile's price sets the runway, and a first shortening of the clock shortens it again through the pile; the carrier is the depth of the market for a seller in a hurry, the cash figure misreads a stock as if its price stood still while the clock ran, and a count corrects it only by putting the clock inside the price and solving for the point where the two agree.

Too expensive to let die: a runway carried by the cost of your death to others, as the only doctor in the district, the engineer who alone knows the plant, the tenant whose leaving would empty a building in a bad market, so counterparties who could call the debt do not, because replacing you costs more than carrying you; the carrier is their replacement cost, the cash figure misreads your clock as yours when it is theirs, and it is corrected only by counting what your death costs someone else; not Forbearance clock, which runs on the creditor's health, since a dying creditor who cannot replace you keeps you alive anyway, and not a leverage, since nothing is exercised.

Weakest wallet: a group's runway is not the pooled cash but the shortest private clock among members who can leave, as the band that ends when the drummer's savings do, the founding team whose firm has eighteen months while a founder's own rent has four, so the group dies at the first departure and not at the pooled zero; the carrier is the members' separate accounts joined to their exit option, the cash figure misreads the pooled balance for the group's time, and counting each wallet corrects it; the monastery, one purse and no private clock, is the case where the pooled count is right, and shows that the illusion is the exit option and not the pooling.

Stamp's clock: a permission that expires on a date no cash extends, as the visa's sixty-day grace, the enlistment, the student's enrolment, the parole, the license that lapses without hours logged, so the death is the stamp's date whenever it falls before the cash's, and every month of cash past it is worth nothing here; the carrier is the issuing authority's calendar, the cash figure misreads money for time where the two do not convert, and no count of money corrects it, since the clock is in a unit money does not buy; not Date bomb, whose step is cleared by paying.

Runway in shots: for anyone who must find a thing before the cash ends, a founder's product, a scientist's result, an actor's part, a prospector's seam, the runway is not months but trials, so halving the burn doubles the months and may leave the shots unchanged if the cut removed the trial capacity, and the same firm with three months is short at one shot a month and long at ten; the carrier is the trial rate, the cash figure misreads time for attempts, and the correction is a change of unit, not a better count; the last item on the route because here the clock is not time at all.

residue.item: Balance read daily: the effective death is the first bad exit accepted, and its date advances with how often the balance is read, since decisions are made against the perceived clock and each reading shrinks it.
residue.why: Unresolved seed: speculative and possibly fertile, but its mechanism is not yet separable from mood, and the panic exit belongs to the psychology fleet; admitting it here would promote a guess about sampling rate to a mechanism. Named in the limits.

residue.item: Bridge that is a pier: financing counted as runway that arrives only on a milestone, so the runway is conditional on the thing the runway was for.
residue.why: Merged into Reach the cliff: the milestone tranche is an asset step whose date is a condition rather than a calendar entry, and the cliff item now lists it; the conditional loop it hints at (runway depends on the result the runway buys) is Runway in shots read backwards, and was not given a third item.

gate: declared modality, recognizable distinction, defensible seriation and conditional relations
limits: Authored conceptual fieldwork, not a taxonomy of insolvency or a model of it; a real case runs several of these at once, and the list claims no coverage.

The seriation is an itinerary of how far the real clock lies from the cash ledger, not a ranking of danger, size, or frequency; map edges are conditional authored claims, and the two loops (Watched burn with Hurry discount, and the front's belief) are analytical, not measured.

The illustrative cases (a bank receivership weekend, a visa grace period, a subcontractor in a housing bust, an officer's mess bill, a district doctor) are simplified to one mechanism each and are not claims about specific histories, firms, or jurisdictions.

Runway in shots assumes the search has a trial rate that a burn cut can remove; where trials are nearly free, as a writer's drafts, the contrast with months disappears, so the item's generality is speculative and its cases are the ones where trials cost money.

Floors under income and the price of a fall in standing belong to the sibling maps; here only the clock. The operator's nerve, the panicked exit that arrives before zero, was left as an unresolved seed rather than admitted, since its mechanism is not yet separable from mood. Adjacent to clocks-that-are-not-clocks, which reads durations off states; every item here is a clock read against the cash figure, and adds what the figure misreads.

neighbors.left: Forbearance clock: a debt with no schedule, as the family loan, the supplier who lets the invoice slide, the tax authority that has not yet noticed, the credit line uncalled, is due at the creditor's discretion, and the creditor's discretion runs on the creditor's own runway, so the debt is patient exactly until the creditor is in trouble, which is when you are; the carrier is the creditor's clock, the cash figure misreads an uncalled debt as not due, and no count of your own ledger corrects it, since the due date lives in someone else's; Receivable from the dying on the other side of the sheet.
neighbors.right: Too expensive to let die: a runway carried by the cost of your death to others, as the only doctor in the district, the engineer who alone knows the plant, the tenant whose leaving would empty a building in a bad market, so counterparties who could call the debt do not, because replacing you costs more than carrying you; the carrier is their replacement cost, the cash figure misreads your clock as yours when it is theirs, and it is corrected only by counting what your death costs someone else; not Forbearance clock, which runs on the creditor's health, since a dying creditor who cannot replace you keeps you alive anyway, and not a leverage, since nothing is exercised.
neighbors.separating_case: A supplier in its own trouble, calling every uncalled invoice it holds, who nevertheless carries one customer because that customer is the only outlet for a line the supplier cannot sell elsewhere. Under Forbearance clock alone the debt is called, since the creditor's clock has run out; under Too expensive to let die it is not, since the creditor's replacement cost exceeds the carry. The reverse case separates them the other way: a flush supplier who can replace you tomorrow keeps forbearing out of habit, which is the forbearance clock running on the creditor's health with no dependence at all.

checks.boundary_case: A sales pipeline counted as revenue is out: it is a miscount of cash, an error in the figure itself, and the map assumes the figure is right and asks what a right figure still misreads. The part of the pipeline that is a mechanism, the buyer whose diligence finds the runway and waits, is already Watched burn. Optimism is not a carrier.
checks.form_inference: The map shows a loop the sequence conceals: Watched burn → Hurry discount, where terms tighten on seeing the burn, the pile fetches less, and the hurried sale is itself seen, so the fixed point the discount could solve for inside one ledger moves once the solving is watched. It shows an incompatibility between neighbors, Watched burn and The front, where a cut that is seen ends the runway it was meant to extend, so past a point the operator cannot hold both. It shows a fork at Date bomb → Stamp's clock, where every dated death splits by whether cash converts to time. It shows a passage between levels at Lien of blood → Weakest wallet, where a person's corrected clock becomes the coalition's minimum. It shows a synchronization at Receivable from the dying → Forbearance clock, where two columns counted separately fail as one event. And it shows a second incompatibility at Near the pole → Runway in shots, where the same cut lengthens the runway in one unit and shortens it in the other.
checks.target_preserved: Self-read only. Each item names a distinct carrier and a distinct misread, and the answer to the live question is carried by the route rather than asserted: three grades of correction, with the hinge at the point where counting better becomes counting what others count. The strange members (a runway that ends on the day of discovery, a clock held by the creditor's dependence, a group that dies at its poorest member, a runway in trials rather than time) are kept as mechanisms and not softened into advice about cash management.

next_crossfield_opening: Clocks counted in the wrong unit: connect Runway in shots and Stamp's clock with clocks-that-are-not-clocks and pivot-invariants; ask what other quantities a runway is really counted in (trials, permissions, the body, standing), which of them convert to money at any rate at all, and whether an operator who counts in the right unit can still be killed by a counterparty who counts in months.

gaps: The declared type was narrower than the map: Near the pole, Burn you cannot put down and Reach the cliff concern the runway's response to a cut or its worth rather than its length, and Stamp's clock, The back and Runway in shots are deaths that are not defaults; the strongest items broke the type, so the type was widened to cover worth and response to the operator's own moves rather than the members cut.
accepted: Reach the cliff: an asset that arrives as a step, as the vesting date, the pension's twentieth year, the bonus paid in March, the tranche released on a milestone, so the runway's worth is a step in its length, a race whose prize is a jump, and the whole loss is quitting three weeks early; the carrier is the payer's schedule, the cash figure misreads a binary as a slope, since the months before the cliff are worth nothing on their own and everything as a bridge; the same calendar as Date bomb read upward, and distinct in what it makes the operator do, since a step down is cleared by having the cash at the date while a step up is raced for by spending whatever reaches the date, so a cut that lengthens the months and misses the date is a loss and not a gain; a permission that arrives on a date, as naturalization at year five, is Stamp's clock read upward and not this.

Forbearance clock: a debt with no schedule, as the family loan, the supplier who lets the invoice slide, the tax authority that has not yet noticed, the credit line uncalled, is due at the creditor's discretion, and the creditor's discretion runs on the creditor's own runway, so the debt is patient exactly until the creditor is in trouble, which need not be when you are, and is when you are whenever the two of you share weather; the carrier is the creditor's clock, the cash figure misreads an uncalled debt as not due, and no count of your own ledger corrects it, since the due date lives in someone else's; Receivable from the dying on the other side of the sheet.

Too expensive to let die: a runway carried by the cost of your death to others, as the only doctor in the district, the engineer who alone knows the plant, the tenant whose leaving would empty a building in a bad market, so counterparties who could call the debt do not, because replacing you costs more than carrying you; the carrier is their replacement cost, the cash figure misreads your clock as yours when it is theirs, and it is corrected only by counting what your death costs someone else; not Forbearance clock, which runs on the creditor's health, since a creditor in trouble who cannot replace you keeps you alive for as long as it expects a future in which to need you, though a creditor in receivership has no replacement cost, since it has no future to replace you in, and its receiver calls the debt; and not a leverage, since nothing is exercised.

Any-town skill: a skill that is cash in any town lengthens the runway to the time it takes to move, while a skill that is cash only here shortens it to the cash, as the nurse or the welder against the fixer who knows this council, the session player known in this scene, the courtier; the carrier is the geography of the market for the skill, the cash figure misreads the pile for the pump, and it is corrected only by counting where the skill sells and at what discount, which is a count of a market you are not yet in; not a floor under income, which is what the skill fetches, since here only where it fetches it matters, and the location of the floor is what sets the clock.

Runway in shots: for anyone who must find a thing before the cash ends, a founder's product, a scientist's result, an actor's part, a prospector's seam, the runway is not months but trials, so halving the burn doubles the months and may leave the shots unchanged if the cut removed the trial capacity, and the same firm with three months is short at one shot a month and long at ten; the carrier is the trial rate, the cash figure misreads time for attempts, and the correction is a change of unit, not a better count; here the clock is not time at all, so no count in months, however good, touches it.

residue.item: Any-town skill's original discriminator, 'adjacent to the floors under income, which the sibling map keeps'.
residue.why: Repaired as the critic asked, but on the critic's second ground only: the item's correction is a count of wages in another town, so it belongs in the counterparty grade, and a boundary belongs in the item. The critic's first ground, that no floors map exists in the atlas or this fleet's directory, is wrong: survival-floors.json sits in the same directory; the limit in boundary_claim now names it.

residue.item: Forbearance clock's 'which is when you are'.
residue.why: Softened to a condition (shared weather) rather than preserved, because the critic showed cases where it fails (an audit cycle, a solvent relative's sudden need) and the map's own edge from Receivable from the dying already carried the condition; a modality repair, not a domestication, since the carrier (the creditor's clock) is untouched.

residue.item: Runway in shots' closing clause 'the last item on the route because here the clock is not time at all'.
residue.why: Positional text removed from the item at the critic's request; the mechanism and the closing claim that no count in months touches it are kept.

limits: The type now admits mechanisms about the runway's worth and its response to the operator's own moves, not only its length; the map still assumes the cash figure itself is right and asks what a right figure misreads, so miscounts of cash (pipelines, stretched payables) remain out.
seed: Lead-time floors: the last months of a runway are spent buying the next one, a raise that takes six months, a job hunt, a move, so a death line sits above zero drawn by a counterparty's latency rather than by the wind-down bill. Cost of the coffin has the floor (drawn by the cost of stopping), Any-town skill has the move time (a runway lengthened to the time it takes to relocate), and Watched burn has the investor who waits, but nothing in the map holds the general mechanism that a runway must contain the time it takes to replace itself, that this time is set by someone else's decision cycle, and that it is the floor operators actually die on ('you are dead at six months, not zero'). It would sit in the second grade beside Watched burn, and the probe is small: for ten firms that raised, subtract the days from first pitch to wire from the months of runway they reported at first pitch, and see how many were already below zero.
